materials.cover_letter:
I have spent my career building AI workflows and then sitting with the customers who rely on them. When I saw the Forward Deployed Engineer role at Figma, it matched the work I have been doing for seven years: understanding technical environments, leading setup and configuration, and debugging issues in real time.

At Redwood, I built FlareGuard, an AI content validation suite that cut escalations by 70-80%. I redesigned a 200-article help portal with role-aware navigation and automated a PDF pipeline that finally resolved a years-long customer complaint. At Bird, I migrated 500+ Zendesk articles and built an in-app help system that shipped every release.

I do the hands-on work of deployment, discovery, and cross-functional coordination. Your customers need someone who can map their workflows, identify blockers, and get them running on Make Local without friction. That is exactly what I do. I would welcome the conversation.

short_answers.Why Figma?: I'm drawn to Figma's commitment to bridging design and engineering through tools like Make Local. My experience building AI-driven workflows to simplify complex technical environments aligns perfectly with enabling customers to adopt Figma's developer-facing features. I've seen how impactful clear implementation support and debugging guidance can be, and I'm excited to bring that expertise to Figma's strategic customer deployments.
short_answers.Tell us about yourself: I'm an AI Workflow Engineer with a strong foundation in technical documentation and customer-facing problem-solving. At Redwood, I built FlareGuard, an AI content validation system that cut escalations by 70–80% by automatically detecting documentation bugs. I thrive at the intersection of engineering and customer success—leading technical discovery, debugging codebase environments, and synthesizing feedback to improve developer workflows. I'm looking to apply that blend of technical depth and customer empathy to Figma's Forward Deployed Engineering team.
